title: Why does one yawn make everyone yawn?
topic: Why do you yawn when someone else yawns?

lines: Ever wonder why a single yawn can make the whole room sigh?

beats.title: What a yawn does
lines: Yawning helps swap stale air for fresh, but that alone doesn’t spread it.
It often comes with a stretch that readies muscles for quick action.
Research shows contagious yawning links to brain cooling and mirrors our empathy.
A 2017 brain‑stimulation study found motor cortex excitability predicts who will yawn next.

beats.title: Animals that yawn together
lines: Wolves and dogs also catch yawns, especially from close pack members.
The stronger the social bond, the faster the response, hinting at an empathy link.
Next time you hear a yawn, notice who’s nearby—your brain may be syncing with theirs!
Try holding your breath first—you might stop the chain.

sources.claim: Contagious yawning may be linked to empathy and social bonding
Wolves show contagious yawning that correlates with social bond strength
Motor cortex excitability predicts contagious yawning propensity
Domestic dogs catch human yawns, suggesting cross‑species contagion
